decisions.reason: The accelerator program costs little and was visibly promoted, which favors keeping it, but it lies furthest from the core machinery business and has no reported results to justify it, so dropping it is nearly as likely as keeping it.

The bio-based bitumen binder is a publicly announced flagship of the CO2-negative direction with sunk development investment, so management will keep it and attribute slow uptake to an immature market, even though it sits outside the core machinery business.

The WASTX Cleanic is a publicly launched flagship built with partner ERMAFA and close to core competencies, and its sunk co-development costs and visible partnership commitment strongly favor persistence.
The mobile SNOWFLAKE plant is central to the modular, decentralized WASTX strategy and draws directly on core competencies, so it is very unlikely to be dropped.
